domainDescription: Build an enterprise medical research database to manage patient registries, trial logs, dosage configurations, and adverse reactions.

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Welcome to MedCore Research Lab. Our clinical trial tracking system needs a foundation. Create a `patients` table with `patient_id` (INT) and `patient_name` (TEXT).

hints.tier1Concept: Use CREATE TABLE to define a new table and specify columns with their data types inside parentheses.
hints.tier3Solution: CREATE TABLE patients (patient_id INT, patient_name TEXT);

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='patients';

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: First patient enrolled! Insert a record for patient_id 101, name 'Alice Monroe' into the `patients` table.

hints.tier1Concept: Use INSERT INTO to add a new row. Specify column names in parentheses and VALUES in a matching set.
hints.tier2Scaffold:
INSERT INTO patients (patient_id, patient_name)
VALUES (101, 'Alice Monroe');
hints.tier3Solution: INSERT INTO patients (patient_id, patient_name) VALUES (101, 'Alice Monroe');

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM patients WHERE patient_id=101;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Batch-enroll two more patients: patient_id 102 'Bob Chen', and patient_id 103 'Carol Davis'.

hints.tier1Concept: INSERT INTO can accept multiple rows in a single statement by separating each value tuple with a comma.
hints.tier3Solution: INSERT INTO patients (patient_id, patient_name) VALUES (102, 'Bob Chen'), (103, 'Carol Davis');

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM patients;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Run a full audit. Retrieve all records from the `patients` table.

hints.tier1Concept: Use SELECT * FROM to retrieve every column and every row from a table.
hints.tier2Scaffold: SELECT * FROM patients;
hints.tier3Solution: SELECT * FROM patients;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM patients;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Fetch the record for patient 102 only. Use a WHERE clause to filter by patient_id.

hints.tier1Concept: Add a WHERE clause after the table name to filter rows based on a condition.
hints.tier2Scaffold: SELECT * FROM patients WHERE patient_id = ___;
hints.tier3Solution: SELECT * FROM patients WHERE patient_id = 102;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT patient_id, patient_name FROM patients WHERE patient_id = 102;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: A data entry error was found. Update patient 103's name from 'Carol Davis' to 'Carol Davies'.

hints.tier1Concept: Use UPDATE ... SET ... WHERE to modify existing records. Always include a WHERE clause to avoid updating every row.
hints.tier2Scaffold: UPDATE patients SET patient_name = 'Carol Davies' WHERE patient_id = ___;
hints.tier3Solution: UPDATE patients SET patient_name = 'Carol Davies' WHERE patient_id = 103;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT patient_name FROM patients WHERE patient_id=103;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Patient 101 has withdrawn from the trial. Delete their record from the `patients` table.

hints.tier1Concept: Use DELETE FROM with a WHERE clause to remove a specific row.
hints.tier2Scaffold: DELETE FROM patients WHERE patient_id = ___;
hints.tier3Solution: DELETE FROM patients WHERE patient_id = 101;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM patients WHERE patient_id=101;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: The IRB requires adding a `enrollment_date` (TEXT) column to the `patients` table for compliance.

hints.tier1Concept: Use ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN to add a new column to an existing table.
hints.tier2Scaffold: ALTER TABLE patients ADD COLUMN enrollment_date TEXT;
hints.tier3Solution: ALTER TABLE patients ADD COLUMN enrollment_date TEXT;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM pragma_table_info('patients') WHERE name='enrollment_date';

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Insert patient 104 'David Park', enrolled on '2024-01-15'.

hints.tier1Concept: Now that enrollment_date exists, you can include it in your INSERT statement.
hints.tier2Scaffold: INSERT INTO patients (patient_id, patient_name, enrollment_date) VALUES (104, 'David Park', '2024-01-15');
hints.tier3Solution: INSERT INTO patients (patient_id, patient_name, enrollment_date) VALUES (104, 'David Park', '2024-01-15');

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM patients WHERE patient_id=104;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Create a `trials` table with `trial_id` (INT), `trial_name` (TEXT), `phase` (TEXT), and `status` (TEXT).

hints.tier1Concept: Define a new table with multiple columns using CREATE TABLE.
hints.tier3Solution: CREATE TABLE trials (trial_id INT, trial_name TEXT, phase TEXT, status TEXT);

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='trials';

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Add two trials: (1, 'Cardio-Alpha Trial', 'Phase II', 'ACTIVE') and (2, 'Neuro-Beta Study', 'Phase III', 'RECRUITING').

hints.tier1Concept: Use INSERT with multiple value tuples to load multiple rows at once.
hints.tier3Solution: INSERT INTO trials VALUES (1, 'Cardio-Alpha Trial', 'Phase II', 'ACTIVE'), (2, 'Neuro-Beta Study', 'Phase III', 'RECRUITING');

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM trials;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Create an `enrollments` table to link patients to trials: `enrollment_id` (INT), `patient_id` (INT), `trial_id` (INT).

hints.tier1Concept: This is a join table (many-to-many bridge). It stores references to both patients and trials.
hints.tier3Solution: CREATE TABLE enrollments (enrollment_id INT, patient_id INT, trial_id INT);

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='enrollments';

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Enroll patient 102 in trial 1 and patient 104 in trial 2. Use enrollment_ids 1 and 2.

hints.tier1Concept: Insert rows that reference patient_id and trial_id values from other tables.
hints.tier2Scaffold: INSERT INTO enrollments VALUES (1, 102, 1), (2, 104, 2);
hints.tier3Solution: INSERT INTO enrollments VALUES (1, 102, 1), (2, 104, 2);

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM enrollments;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: List every patient's name alongside the trial they are enrolled in. JOIN patients, enrollments, and trials.

hints.tier1Concept: Use INNER JOIN to combine rows from tables where the join condition matches.
hints.tier2Scaffold:
SELECT p.patient_name, t.trial_name
FROM patients p
JOIN enrollments e ON p.patient_id = e.patient_id
JOIN trials t ON e.trial_id = t.trial_id;
hints.tier3Solution: SELECT p.patient_name, t.trial_name FROM patients p JOIN enrollments e ON p.patient_id = e.patient_id JOIN trials t ON e.trial_id = t.trial_id;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM patients p JOIN enrollments e ON p.patient_id = e.patient_id JOIN trials t ON e.trial_id = t.trial_id;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Create a `dosage_logs` table: `log_id` (INT), `patient_id` (INT), `mg_administered` (REAL), `log_timestamp` (TEXT).

hints.tier1Concept: Use REAL for decimal values like milligrams.
hints.tier3Solution: CREATE TABLE dosage_logs (log_id INT, patient_id INT, mg_administered REAL, log_timestamp TEXT);

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='dosage_logs';

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Log three dosage records for patient 102: 50mg at '2024-02-01', 75mg at '2024-02-08', 75mg at '2024-02-15'. Use log_ids 1, 2, 3.

hints.tier1Concept: Insert multiple rows into dosage_logs at once.

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM dosage_logs;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Calculate the total milligrams administered to patient 102 across all logged sessions.

hints.tier1Concept: Use SUM() aggregate function with a WHERE clause to total values for a specific patient.
hints.tier2Scaffold: SELECT SUM(mg_administered) as total_mg FROM dosage_logs WHERE patient_id = ___;
hints.tier3Solution: SELECT SUM(mg_administered) as total_mg FROM dosage_logs WHERE patient_id = 102;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT SUM(mg_administered) as total_mg FROM dosage_logs WHERE patient_id = 102;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Calculate the average dosage and total number of log entries for patient 102.

hints.tier1Concept: Use AVG() for average and COUNT(*) for row count within the same SELECT.
hints.tier2Scaffold: SELECT AVG(mg_administered) as avg_mg, COUNT(*) as sessions FROM dosage_logs WHERE patient_id = 102;
hints.tier3Solution: SELECT AVG(mg_administered) as avg_mg, COUNT(*) as sessions FROM dosage_logs WHERE patient_id = 102;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT AVG(mg_administered) as avg_mg, COUNT(*) as sessions FROM dosage_logs WHERE patient_id = 102;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Add dosage logs for patient 104: (4, 104, 100, '2024-02-01'). Then calculate total dosage grouped by each patient.

hints.tier1Concept: First insert the new row, then use GROUP BY with SUM() to aggregate per patient.
hints.tier2Scaffold:
INSERT INTO dosage_logs VALUES (4, 104, 100, '2024-02-01');
SELECT patient_id, SUM(mg_administered) as total FROM dosage_logs GROUP BY patient_id;
hints.tier3Solution: INSERT INTO dosage_logs VALUES (4, 104, 100, '2024-02-01'); SELECT patient_id, SUM(mg_administered) as total FROM dosage_logs GROUP BY patient_id;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM (SELECT patient_id FROM dosage_logs GROUP BY patient_id);

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Using HAVING, find all patients whose total dosage exceeds 150mg.

hints.tier1Concept: HAVING filters aggregated results, similar to WHERE but applied after GROUP BY.
hints.tier2Scaffold: SELECT patient_id, SUM(mg_administered) as total FROM dosage_logs GROUP BY patient_id HAVING total > ___;
hints.tier3Solution: SELECT patient_id, SUM(mg_administered) as total FROM dosage_logs GROUP BY patient_id HAVING total > 150;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT patient_id, SUM(mg_administered) as total FROM dosage_logs GROUP BY patient_id HAVING total > 150;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: List all dosage log entries for patient 102, ordered chronologically by `log_timestamp` ascending.

hints.tier1Concept: Use ORDER BY column_name ASC to sort results in ascending order.
hints.tier2Scaffold: SELECT * FROM dosage_logs WHERE patient_id = 102 ORDER BY log_timestamp ___;
hints.tier3Solution: SELECT * FROM dosage_logs WHERE patient_id = 102 ORDER BY log_timestamp ASC;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM dosage_logs WHERE patient_id = 102;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Create an `adverse_events` table: `event_id` (INT), `patient_id` (INT), `severity` (TEXT), `description` (TEXT), `event_date` (TEXT).

hints.tier1Concept: Create another table to track side effects. Severity will hold values like LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH.
hints.tier2Scaffold:
CREATE TABLE adverse_events (
  event_id INT,
  patient_id INT,
  severity TEXT,
  description TEXT,
  event_date TEXT
);
hints.tier3Solution: CREATE TABLE adverse_events (event_id INT, patient_id INT, severity TEXT, description TEXT, event_date TEXT);

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='adverse_events';

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Log adverse events: (1, 102, 'LOW', 'Mild nausea', '2024-02-10'), (2, 104, 'HIGH', 'Severe reaction', '2024-02-03').

hints.tier1Concept: Insert the two events with distinct severity levels.
hints.tier3Solution: INSERT INTO adverse_events VALUES (1, 102, 'LOW', 'Mild nausea', '2024-02-10'), (2, 104, 'HIGH', 'Severe reaction', '2024-02-03');

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM adverse_events;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: List all patients and any adverse events they may have. Patients with no events should still appear. Use LEFT JOIN.

hints.tier1Concept: LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table, plus matched rows from the right. Unmatched rows get NULLs.
hints.tier3Solution: SELECT p.patient_name, ae.severity, ae.description FROM patients p LEFT JOIN adverse_events ae ON p.patient_id = ae.patient_id;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM patients p LEFT JOIN adverse_events ae ON p.patient_id = ae.patient_id;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Find all patients who have at least one HIGH severity adverse event, using a subquery.

hints.tier1Concept: Use a subquery inside a WHERE IN (...) clause to filter based on results from another SELECT.
hints.tier3Solution: SELECT * FROM patients WHERE patient_id IN (SELECT patient_id FROM adverse_events WHERE severity = 'HIGH');

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT patient_id FROM patients WHERE patient_id IN (SELECT patient_id FROM adverse_events WHERE severity = 'HIGH');

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Create a view called `high_risk_patients` that selects all patients with HIGH severity adverse events.

hints.tier1Concept: Use CREATE VIEW to define a named virtual table based on a SELECT query.
hints.tier2Scaffold:
CREATE VIEW high_risk_patients AS
  SELECT p.* FROM patients p
  JOIN adverse_events ae ON p.patient_id = ae.patient_id
  WHERE ae.severity = 'HIGH';
hints.tier3Solution: CREATE VIEW high_risk_patients AS SELECT p.* FROM patients p JOIN adverse_events ae ON p.patient_id = ae.patient_id WHERE ae.severity = 'HIGH';

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='view' AND name='high_risk_patients';

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Use a CTE (Common Table Expression) to calculate the average dosage per patient, then select patients whose average exceeds 60mg.

hints.tier1Concept: A CTE is defined with WITH cte_name AS (...) and then referenced like a table in the subsequent SELECT.
hints.tier3Solution: WITH avg_dosage AS (SELECT patient_id, AVG(mg_administered) as avg_mg FROM dosage_logs GROUP BY patient_id) SELECT * FROM avg_dosage WHERE avg_mg > 60;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM (WITH avg_dosage AS (SELECT patient_id, AVG(mg_administered) as avg_mg FROM dosage_logs GROUP BY patient_id) SELECT * FROM avg_dosage WHERE avg_mg > 60);

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Assign a row number to each dosage log entry per patient ordered by timestamp. Use ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY patient_id ORDER BY log_timestamp).

hints.tier1Concept: ROW_NUMBER() is a window function. PARTITION BY resets the count for each group, ORDER BY defines the sequence.
hints.tier3Solution: SELECT patient_id, log_timestamp, mg_administered, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY patient_id ORDER BY log_timestamp) as session_num FROM dosage_logs;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM (SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY patient_id ORDER BY log_timestamp) as rn FROM dosage_logs);

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Compute a running cumulative dosage total per patient sorted chronologically. Use SUM() OVER (PARTITION BY patient_id ORDER BY log_timestamp).

hints.tier1Concept: SUM() as a window function with ORDER BY creates a running total within each partition.
hints.tier3Solution: SELECT patient_id, mg_administered, SUM(mg_administered) OVER (PARTITION BY patient_id ORDER BY log_timestamp) AS running_total FROM dosage_logs;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM (SELECT SUM(mg_administered) OVER (PARTITION BY patient_id ORDER BY log_timestamp) as rt FROM dosage_logs);

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Add a risk classification to adverse events. Use CASE to label severity: HIGH as 'Critical', LOW as 'Monitored', others as 'Unknown'.

hints.tier1Concept: Use CASE WHEN ... THEN ... ELSE ... END to create conditional column values.
hints.tier2Scaffold:
SELECT patient_id, severity,
  CASE severity
    WHEN 'HIGH' THEN 'Critical'
    WHEN 'LOW' THEN 'Monitored'
    ELSE 'Unknown'
  END as risk_level
FROM adverse_events;
hints.tier3Solution: SELECT patient_id, severity, CASE severity WHEN 'HIGH' THEN 'Critical' WHEN 'LOW' THEN 'Monitored' ELSE 'Unknown' END as risk_level FROM adverse_events;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM (SELECT CASE severity WHEN 'HIGH' THEN 'Critical' END as risk_level FROM adverse_events WHERE severity='HIGH');

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Retrieve a list of unique severities recorded in the `adverse_events` table using DISTINCT.

hints.tier1Concept: SELECT DISTINCT eliminates duplicate rows from the result set.
hints.tier2Scaffold: SELECT DISTINCT severity FROM adverse_events;
hints.tier3Solution: SELECT DISTINCT severity FROM adverse_events;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT severity) as count FROM adverse_events;

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Find all patients whose name starts with 'C' using the LIKE operator.

hints.tier1Concept: Use LIKE with a % wildcard to match patterns. 'C%' means any string starting with C.
hints.tier2Scaffold: SELECT * FROM patients WHERE patient_name LIKE 'C%';
hints.tier3Solution: SELECT * FROM patients WHERE patient_name LIKE 'C%';

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT patient_id FROM patients WHERE patient_name LIKE 'C%';

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Optimize query performance. Create an index named `idx_dosage_patient` on the `patient_id` column of `dosage_logs`.

hints.tier1Concept: CREATE INDEX speeds up lookups on frequently-queried columns.
hints.tier2Scaffold: CREATE INDEX idx_dosage_patient ON dosage_logs(patient_id);
hints.tier3Solution: CREATE INDEX idx_dosage_patient ON dosage_logs(patient_id);

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='index' AND name='idx_dosage_patient';

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: Final analytics report: list each patient's name, total dosage, and whether they had any HIGH severity events. Use a LEFT JOIN with aggregation.

hints.tier1Concept: Combine JOIN, GROUP BY, SUM(), and a CASE or MAX() to build a comprehensive report in one query.
hints.tier2Scaffold:
SELECT p.patient_name,
  SUM(dl.mg_administered) as total_dosage,
  MAX(CASE WHEN ae.severity='HIGH' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as had_critical_event
FROM patients p
LEFT JOIN dosage_logs dl ON p.patient_id = dl.patient_id
LEFT JOIN adverse_events ae ON p.patient_id = ae.patient_id
GROUP BY p.patient_id;
hints.tier3Solution: SELECT p.patient_name, SUM(dl.mg_administered) as total_dosage, MAX(CASE WHEN ae.severity='HIGH' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as had_critical_event FROM patients p LEFT JOIN dosage_logs dl ON p.patient_id = dl.patient_id LEFT JOIN adverse_events ae ON p.patient_id = ae.patient_id GROUP BY p.patient_id;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM (SELECT p.patient_name FROM patients p LEFT JOIN dosage_logs dl ON p.patient_id = dl.patient_id GROUP BY p.patient_id);

curriculumMatrix.narrativeBriefing: The trial is closed. Drop the `enrollments` table as it is no longer needed for this archive.

hints.tier1Concept: Use DROP TABLE to permanently remove a table from the database.
hints.tier2Scaffold: DROP TABLE enrollments;
hints.tier3Solution: DROP TABLE enrollments;

curriculumMatrix.verificationQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='enrollments';
